subtasks.description: Create the Iteration 1 project baseline by adding pyproject configuration, minimal dependencies, and runnable package skeletons for speedster and agent modules.

functional: pyproject.toml declares the required Iteration 1 dependencies (pydantic, httpx, redis, fastapi, uvicorn, typer) and runnable package entry points for speedster and agent.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by keeping speedster and agent package boundaries separate with explicit module responsibilities.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by adding only the build/runtime setup required for Iteration 1 execution.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover package-loading behavior introduced by this subtask, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: This subtask bootstraps the two package roots and the build manifest, so only these entry points are needed.

subtasks.description: Implement role configuration models in speedster/config.py with explicit model mapping for em, engineer, and qa plus strict runtime validation.

functional: speedster/config.py defines explicit per-role model mapping and rejects invalid or missing role/model configuration at runtime.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by isolating schema definition from loading and validation behavior in config.py.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by limiting configuration scope to Iteration 1 role-model mapping requirements.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover valid and invalid configuration scenarios, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: config.py is the sole module under change and pyproject.toml defines the dependency it pulls from.

subtasks.description: Implement agent/server.py FastAPI service exposing only /work and /health with typed request/response contracts and deterministic error handling.

functional: agent/server.py exposes only /work and /health endpoints with documented request/response models and deterministic non-200 error responses for invalid input.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by separating transport DTOs, service logic, and error mapping responsibilities.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by avoiding extra endpoints or orchestration logic outside Iteration 1 needs.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover /work and /health success and failure paths, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: server.py implements the endpoints, main.py wires the server, and config.py defines the role identity the server exposes.

subtasks.description: Implement strict output validation in speedster/output_validator.py for EM breakdown payloads and QA review payloads with deterministic rejection on malformed JSON.

functional: speedster/output_validator.py enforces strict JSON schema validation for EM breakdown and QA review outputs and returns deterministic validation errors for malformed payloads.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by keeping schema definitions, parser behavior, and error translation isolated and testable.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by supporting only Iteration 1 output contracts without speculative schema extensions.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover valid, invalid-shape, and invalid-JSON cases, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: output_validator.py is the module under change; config.py declares the payload contract sources it must enforce.

subtasks.description: Implement orchestrator HTTP client in speedster/agent_client.py for role-targeted calls to /work and /health with Iteration 1 timeout and retry behavior.

functional: speedster/agent_client.py can call /work and /health for em, engineer, and qa endpoints with explicit timeout and retry behavior appropriate for Iteration 1.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by separating request construction, transport execution, and response parsing concerns.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by using a minimal retry strategy and avoiding premature multi-replica load-balancing logic.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover success, timeout, and retry cases, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: agent_client.py is the module under change; it must call the contract defined in server.py using role config.

subtasks.description: Create canonical Iteration 1 task fixture in tasks/task-001/task.json aligned with orchestrator and validator contracts for the vertical slice scenario.

functional: tasks/task-001/task.json exists and is valid against the Iteration 1 task input shape used by the orchestrator and validators.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by keeping fixture schema and orchestration logic decoupled.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by containing only fields required for Iteration 1 execution.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover fixture loading and schema compatibility, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: The fixture is the file under change; the orchestrator and validator are the consumers whose contract it must satisfy.

subtasks.description: Implement a minimal orchestrator state machine in speedster/orchestrator.py for one task and one subtask through EM planning, Engineer implementation, and QA approve/rework loop.

functional: speedster/orchestrator.py executes one-task flow EM then Engineer then QA and repeats Engineer rework when QA rejects until approved or an explicit terminal state.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by separating state-transition logic, external-client interactions, and validation concerns.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by limiting control flow to Iteration 1 single-task and single-subtask behavior.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover happy path and one reject-then-approve path for state transitions, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: The orchestrator coordinates the client, validator, and config, so those four files are the minimal sufficient set.

subtasks.description: Implement end-to-end integration tests proving task completion occurs only after QA approval, including at least one reject-then-pass cycle.

functional: An integration test executes the Iteration 1 vertical slice and asserts task status becomes done only after QA returns approved true, including one reject-then-pass cycle.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by using reusable fixtures and isolating test responsibilities.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by validating only Iteration 1 behavior without introducing non-required scenario breadth.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover the approval-gate behavior, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: The integration test exercises the orchestrator via the agent client, with tests/ as the output location.

subtasks.description: Add structured observability fields to record role, model identifier, call latency, and QA round number for each orchestration step.

functional: Execution logs and metrics include role, model identifier, latency, and QA round fields for EM, Engineer, and QA calls in a single run.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by separating telemetry formatting from orchestration decision logic.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by introducing only Iteration 1 telemetry fields required by the exit criteria.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover telemetry payload structure and emission points, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: Telemetry is emitted by the orchestrator and agent client and aggregated by the performance tracker.

subtasks.description: Produce an Iteration 1 runbook and lightweight verification helper that executes two consecutive reproducible runs and captures proof of role-specific models and the QA feedback loop.

functional: A runbook documents the exact command sequence to execute Iteration 1 twice consecutively and collect reproducibility evidence for role-model mapping and the QA reject-then-pass path.
acceptance_criteria.solid: The implementation adheres to SOLID principles by separating setup, execution orchestration, and result-validation responsibilities.
acceptance_criteria.yagni_kiss: The implementation adheres to YAGNI and KISS by including only Iteration 1 operational checks and avoiding non-required automation features.
acceptance_criteria.testing: Well-designed unit tests cover verification-helper parsing and validation logic, with minimum unit test coverage of 80%+ for touched modules.

subtasks.context_rationale: Runbook lives in README.md and references PLAN.md criteria; the verification helper is exercised from tests/.
